manifest.name: Online Event Booths
manifest.summary: Events, display your booths on your website

models._description: (inherit) booth website page + exhibition map + booth menu

behavioral_notes.observation: The public storefront page (http, auth=public, website=True) renders website_event_booth.event_booth_registration. _prepare_booth_main_values reads event.sudo().event_booth_category_available_ids (categories that still have available booths) and event_booth_ids, picks a default/selected booth category, and passes hide_sponsors + open event slots. has_access('read') is checked first (raising Forbidden), and the public ir.rule (event_id.website_published=True) plus the access_event_booth_public read grant make backend event.booth rows browsable by anonymous visitors. This is the exhibitor-facing 'Become exhibitor' page; the controller assembles the booth catalog, not metadata.

Booth picking is a two-hop POST->GET. booth/register (POST) re-parses request.httprequest.form.getlist('event_booth_ids') (because request.params only keeps the first checkbox) and redirects to booth/register_form with booth_ids (comma-joined) + booth_category_id in the query string. booth/register_form (GET) browses the chosen event.booth.category and the selected event.booth recordset, then _prepare_booth_contact_form_values pre-fills default_contact from request.env.user.partner_id (logged user) or website.visitor._get_visitor_from_request() (anonymous, by email), and renders website_event_booth.event_booth_registration_details (the contact form). The booth-category selection drives which booths are offered. None of this PRG hand-off is in metadata.

The confirm POST is the bridge's core write. _get_requested_booths re-queries event.booth as sudo with event_id + state='available' + id in posted ids, and rejects the order (returns empty) if any requested id is gone or the booths span more than one booth_category_id (anti-tamper / race guard). _check_booth_registration_values blocks empty selections (boothError) and, for public users, refuses an email that already matches an existing res.partner (existingPartnerError -> sign-in prompt). _prepare_booth_registration_partner_values resolves the exhibitor: for public users event.sudo()._partner_find_from_emails_single creates/finds a res.partner from contact_email with name/phone; logged users reuse user.partner_id. It then calls booths.action_confirm(booth_values), which (in event_booth) flips each booth state available->unavailable and posts a booked note on the event chatter. So an anonymous visitor assigns and books real event.booth rows. Returns a JSON success payload (event_name + contact) consumed by the JS. Invisible to metadata.

Two public jsonrpc routes back the live UX. /event/booth/check_availability browses the posted event_booth_ids and returns the subset whose is_available is False, letting the JS flag race-lost booths in red before final submit. /event/booth_category/get_available_booths searches event.booth (event_id + booth_category_id + state='available') and returns [{id,name}], so the client repopulates the booth checkbox list when the exhibitor switches category without a full page reload. Both run sudo. This client/server availability protocol is pure controller code.

The event.event inherit adds an exhibition_map Image, a booth_menu Boolean (computed from event_type.booth_menu or website_menu) and booth_menu_ids (website.event.menu filtered menu_type='booth'). _get_website_menu_entries appends a ('Become exhibitor', '/event/<slug>/booth', ... 'booth') entry, and _update_website_menus / _get_menu_type_field_matching / _get_menu_update_fields hook the generic website_event menu-sync so toggling booth_menu creates or unlinks the per-event 'Become exhibitor' website.menu + website.event.menu rows (menu_type 'booth', ondelete cascade). copy_event_menus re-parents booth menus on event duplication. A live-navigation side-effect not in the schema.

1 JS file (booth_registration.js) registers a public.interactions BoothRegistration on .o_wbooth_registration plus 1 client XML template file; no OWL components, 3 web.assets_frontend entries. The interaction drives category radio change -> rpc get_available_booths (cached per category) -> client-side renderAt of event_booth_checkbox_list, disables submit until a booth is checked, calls rpc check_availability before submit (flags unavailable booths red), then on the contact step posts FormData to booth/confirm via http_service.post and renders event_booth_registration_complete inline on success or shows boothError/boothCategoryError/existingPartnerError messages. Entirely client-side, outside Python metadata.

it_architecture.application: website_event_booth (Online Event Booths website bridge application component, extends website_event + event_booth)
software_services: /event/<event>/booth -- public booth storefront page (catalog by available category)
/event/<event>/booth/register -- POST booth selection, PRG redirect to contact form
/event/booth/check_availability (jsonrpc) -- return unavailable booths among a selection
/event/booth_category/get_available_booths (jsonrpc) -- list available booths for a category
information_flows: side-effect: POST /booth/confirm -> _partner_find_from_emails_single (create/find res.partner) -> event.booth.action_confirm -> booth state available->unavailable + booked note on event chatter (event_booth)
side-effect: event.booth_menu toggle -> _update_website_menus -> create/unlink website.menu + website.event.menu ('booth') 'Become exhibitor' entry
flow: category radio -> jsonrpc get_available_booths -> client booth list; pre-submit jsonrpc check_availability -> race-loss flagging
guard: _get_requested_booths re-checks state='available' + single booth_category + ids match (anti-tamper); public email collision -> existingPartnerError sign-in prompt

capabilities: Publish Booths to the Event Website (exhibition map, 'Become exhibitor' page)
Online Booth Catalog Browsing by Category (available booths only)
Online Self-Service Booth Selection (category -> booth checkbox list)
Capture Exhibitor Contact Details (anonymous & logged visitors)
Confirm & Book a Booth Online (partner find/create -> action_confirm)
Live Booth Availability Checking (race-loss & category refresh)
value_streams: Browse-to-Booked-Booth: exhibitor opens /event/<id>/booth -> selects booth category -> picks available booth(s) -> submits contact form -> booth/confirm finds/creates partner and action_confirm books the booth (available->unavailable) -> inline success confirmation
policies: 1 record rule: public/portal may read event.booth only where event_id.website_published=True (frontend exposure gate)
4 access rules: public/portal/employee read on event.booth, public read on event.booth.category; no write/create for public (booking done sudo via action_confirm)
anti-tamper guard: _get_requested_booths requires booths still available, ids match, and exactly one booth_category before confirming
public-email collision policy: an existing res.partner email is refused (existingPartnerError) and the visitor is asked to sign in
booth_menu auto-managed from event_type.booth_menu / website_menu, syncing the 'Become exhibitor' website navigation
metrics: available booth categories per event (event_booth_category_available_ids, frontend-facing)
online booth bookings (event.booth flipped to unavailable via /booth/confirm)
booth availability checks / category refresh rpc volume (storefront engagement)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_event_booth is the BRIDGE that fuses two value networks: website_event (the public web-presence/registration channel) and event_booth (the booth-capacity mediation layer of the event network). Its reason to exist is to turn the website into the public booth SALES channel -- it publishes booths as a 'Become exhibitor' storefront page, operates the catalog of available booth categories, and runs the self-service /event/<id>/booth -> /booth/register -> /booth/confirm flow that finds/creates a res.partner and books real event.booth rows (state available->unavailable) from anonymous visitors. This is mediating-technology logic (Stabell & Fjeldstad value network): connecting an open population of prospective exhibitors to a fixed pool of event booth capacity and matching them, with live availability rollups and race-loss guards -- not a sequential input->output transformation (chain) nor case-by-case problem solving (shop). activity_class is primary because online exhibitor acquisition and booth booking is a customer-facing demand/sell activity, not back-office support. apqc_category 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services is the closest PCF home, inherited from both parents: the bridge's purpose is the public market/sell motion -- marketing booth space and selling/allocating it to exhibitors online; the paid checkout/invoicing portion lives in the separate event_booth_sale addon, so this module covers the website catalog + online assignment portion of that sell process.

standard_capabilities: public 'Become exhibitor' booth page at /event/<id>/booth with exhibition map and booth-category catalog
auto-generated per-event booth website menu (menu_type 'booth') from booth_menu / event-type flag
online booth-category selection with live available-booth list (jsonrpc, no page reload)
two-step self-service booking: pick booths -> exhibitor contact form -> confirm
anonymous-friendly partner resolution (find/create res.partner from contact email) on confirm
live availability/race-loss checking and inline success confirmation
typical_fits: trade shows / conferences letting exhibitors reserve a stand online
capacity-limited booth catalogs with live sold-out enforcement on the website
marketing-driven exhibitor landing pages reusing the event website + booth categories
common_gaps: paid online booth checkout / invoicing and per-category pricing (needs event_booth_sale)
visual floor-plan / spatial stand picker (not in standard -- only a checkbox list)
custom exhibitor onboarding fields/steps beyond contact name/email/phone
approval workflow before a booth is booked (confirm is immediate available->unavailable)

Whether a reserved/pending intermediate booth state is introduced under paid checkout, vs the binary available->unavailable used here.
